title: MEA, MOCA & Friends
hook: Five altitude acronyms guard every airway. Know who does what.

scenes.narration: Airway leg across the mountains. The chart shows M E A eleven thousand... and underneath, with a star: nine thousand three hundred. Two altitudes for one piece of sky, kid. They are not interchangeable.
Both altitudes clear the rocks. So what does the M E A give you that the M O C A doesn't? Commit.

Navigation signal, the whole segment. M E A: obstacles AND nav coverage, fix to fix. M O C A: obstacles too — but V O R signal only within twenty-two miles. Why twenty-two? V O R is line of sight; down low, that's as far as the signal is guaranteed to reach.

The rest of the family: M R A — high enough to RECEIVE an off-route fix. M C A — cross the fix AT or above it, so climb early. O R O C A — off-airway clearance by quadrant, a thousand feet, two in the mountains, no signal promises.
Eyes off the chart. M E A versus M O C A — the one-sentence difference. Out loud.
M E A does both jobs. M O C A clears rocks with short-range signal. M R A hears the fix, M C A crosses it high. Granite doesn't grade on a curve, kid.
From the lost-comm lesson — the radio's dead over these same mountains. Your altitude is the highest of which three? Go.
Ninety-one one seventy-seven sets the floor. Literally.

quiz.question: MEA 11,000 and MOCA *9,300 on the same segment. The MEA additionally guarantees:
choices: Nav signal coverage for the whole segment
quiz.explanation: MEA covers both obstruction clearance and navigation signal coverage between fixes; MOCA's signal guarantee stops at 22 NM from the VOR.

quiz.question: The MOCA assures VOR navigation signal coverage only within:
quiz.explanation: MOCA provides full obstacle clearance but signal coverage only within 22 NM of the VOR. Below the MEA, that's the catch.

quiz.question: An MCA published at a fix means you must:
choices: Cross that fix at or above the MCA
Begin your descent at that fix
Be able to receive the fix at that altitude
quiz.explanation: MCA is a crossing restriction — start the climb early so you cross at or above it (MRA is the reception altitude).
